title: Viewport: another setup's WCS is drawn in the wrong place when the part is aligned differently

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Reported by the maintainer (filed by an agent), 2026-11-09, with screenshots (v0.15.0 · 2e77f805).

**What happens:** with two setups (Setup1 selected, Setup2 active) and the part aligned to the plane differently between them, the viewport draws the part in the shown setup's alignment. One WCS triad sits at the part's origin crosshair. The other setup's WCS triad, though, is drawn far off at the stock's outer top corner, not on the part. So when WCS triads stay visible across setups, a setup's WCS doesn't stay where it belongs on the part.

**Expected:** a setup's WCS is a point fixed on the part (its origin crosshair, in relation to the part's placement on that setup's plane). When the viewport shows the part in setup A's alignment, every visible WCS from another setup B is drawn through the same transform the part went through: B's WCS in B's frame, mapped by `setup_relative::transform_between(B, A)` (or via the part frame), so it sticks to the same physical spot on the part. If the transform between the two setups isn't known or is refused, don't draw B's triad in a misleading place: hide it or show it greyed with a "not in this setup's frame" note.

**Likely cause:** the WCS gizmo for non-shown setups is drawn from its stored world position (in its own setup's frame), with no mapping into the shown setup's part alignment.

**Done means:**
- A test with two setups whose part alignments differ (e.g. a flip or a quarter turn), where the viewport model places setup B's WCS at the same part-relative point as the part's crosshair for B.
- Switching which setup is shown keeps each WCS on its spot on the part.
- An unmappable WCS is hidden or flagged, never drawn somewhere wrong.

Related: #330 (lay the face on the plane, reopened), #316 (stored transform between setups), #342 (one WCS per setup).

title: Main is red: structural shell tests expect the real version on the pinned toolbar label

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
**What happens:** on main, `egui_app::tests::structural::shell_structure_dark` and `shell_structure_light` fail. They look for the toolbar label `v0.15.0 · test` (built from `env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")`, structural.rs:75), but since #450 the toolbar shows the test-pinned `v0.0.0 · test`. Found by the review of PR #524.

**Cause:** two merges that each passed alone: PR #359 (#255) added the structural tests with the real version, and PR #450 (#449) pinned the toolbar version to "0.0.0" under cfg(test).

**Fix:** build the expected label from the same source the toolbar uses (`crate::build_info::toolbar_lines(false).0`), so a version bump or a re-pin can't split them again.

**Done means:** both structural tests pass on main.

Depends on: #534.

Off by default (D6). When on, tab count, width and position are required, with no invented default. The main cut leaves the tabs; a later cut-off pass removes them. Slug analysis from the wire verify sub-issue refuses an unsupported slug unless tabs or a capture are set.

Upper and lower profiles given separately, paired into moves whose pose spans from the lower point to the paired upper point (D2). Part of #290 (design decisions D1-D10 in its research comment).

Depends on: #533, #534.

A constant taper angle expressed as the move pose (D2): the wire direction tilted by the angle toward the stated side. The post writes the taper the way the dialect's codes state (angle words or UV), per D5.

Refusals: an angle above the machine's stated maximum (naming the op and the angle), and a UV point outside the travel band or guide reach.

**Done means:** a 3° die posts and verifies, a 30° request on a 15° machine is refused by name, and the CL golden shows the poses.

title: EDM: machine kinds wire_edm and sinker_edm in the .mch schema

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: P?
labels.description: Paused: never picked until the maintainer sets a real priority

body:
Part of #290 (design decisions D1-D10 in its research comment).

Add `general.kind` values `wire_edm` and `sinker_edm` to the machine model (`crates/post/src/machine`), its mirror and `assets/machines/AGENTS.md`. Unknown kinds still refuse.
- **Wire:** U/V travel bands, lower and upper guide heights, maximum taper angle (degrees), supported wire diameters, an `edm.awt` flag and an optional Z.
- **Sinker:** Z travel, orbit capability (the list of supported pattern kinds with the machine's word for each), maximum orbit radius, pickup/reference method and electrode holder limits.
- Absent keys stay "not stated". Ship one wire and one sinker library file with the dialect and condition tables empty (D4/D5).

**Done means:** both kinds parse and round-trip, a garbled key refuses the file by name, an unknown kind still refuses, and the checker reports absent EDM keys as not stated. Pinned by machine tests.
